paper_citation: Mason Edgar, DCT Image Steganography software implementation, GitHub commit 20da3e1e4d6b48dbcbe241c776ee156995bb65fe.

payload_contract.content: same preregistered progressive raw-secret bitplanes used by FINAL-5J-v1

distortion_contract.repair: up to four deterministic clean-only feedback passes that correct measured spatial-round-trip DCT residuals to the nearest desired-parity QIM lattice point
distortion_contract.selection: clean-valid candidate with realized cover-stego PSNR closest to the declared target

attack_contract.implementation: shared FINAL-5J attack functions and frozen seeds

adaptations.description: A self-contained orthonormal DCT scalar-QIM implementation replaces the reference repository's positive-coefficient LSB routine. The reference commit establishes DCT-domain lineage, not author-equivalent execution.
Thirty-two frozen low/mid-frequency AC positions provide exact capacity for the full 131,072-bit raw secret.
QIM delta is selected from a frozen list by closest realized PSNR, and only clean-bit-exact candidates are admissible.
A bounded parity-preserving repair strengthens only coefficients that fail clean uint8 round-trip extraction.

The required target-server two-pair dry run exposed that blind ±2-delta repair did not converge on one frozen dry-run cover. Before any main-study execution, repair was corrected to use the measured uint8 spatial round-trip DCT residual and move only the mismatched coefficient to the nearest desired-parity QIM lattice point. The frozen delta list, four-pass bound, capacity, payload, and selection rule are unchanged.

limitations: This is a canonical engineering baseline, not a claim of exact reproduction of a peer-reviewed paper.
No ECC or semantic Base/Detail layer exists; those fields are not_applicable.
The exact selected delta is cover-dependent but chosen only from the frozen candidate set before attacks.
Repository CI and target-server dry-run verification are required after the engineering repair amendment and before production execution.
